newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPOSED COMPAGNONI TAKES GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPOSED COMPAGNONI TAKES GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Italian world and Olympic champion Deborah Compagnoni clinched her first giant slalom victory of the Alpine skiing season on Friday after an aggressive but composed performance on a bumpy German piste.

Compagnoni, who had twice finished second in the discipline in Maribor, Slovenia, and the Austrian resort of Soelden, clocked an aggregate two minutes 8.45 seconds in the fourth giant slalom of the season, according to provisional results.

It was the 26-year-old Italian's second World Cup victory of the season after she won a slalom in Semmering, Austria, on December 29, her first every victory on the circuit in the technical discipline.
Austria's Anita Wachter was second in 2:09.61 with Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg third in 2:09.92 in the first World Cup event in the German resort for six years.
In cold conditions, Compagnoni showed good rhythm and control through a tight set of gates to take a 1.08 seconds lead ahead of Germany's Katja Seizinger after the first run.
After Seizinger fell in the second run, the Italian skied a smooth second run of 1:04.76 to make sure of victory.
It was a bad day for Seizinger and Italy's Sabina Panzanini, who both started the day equal top of the World Cup giant slalom standings.
Panzanini, who had won two of the three previous giant slaloms, looked uncomfortable on the course which was icy in parts and she was unable to make an impact after finishing 19th in the first run.
